extracted.intended_audience: Researchers considering or preparing applications for European Research Council (ERC) grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility criteria for applicants to the European Research Council's suite of grants (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced, Proof of Concept, Synergy), plus pointers to supporting resources. Intended to help researchers decide which ERC grant to target and where to find application guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Starting Grants eligibility & selection
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 2-7 years of experience since the completion of their PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility combines career stage (2–7 years post-PhD), evidence of promising scientific track-record, and the quality of the research proposal (described as 'excellent'). Use annual Work Programme/Information for Applicants for call-specific details.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Consolidator Grants eligibility & selection
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers with 7-12 years of experience since completion of PhD, a scientific track record showing great promise and an excellent research proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines career stage (7–12 years post-PhD), demonstrated promising track-record, and an excellent research proposal. Applicants should consult the Work Programme/Information for Applicants for further call-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Advanced Grants eligibility & selection
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for active researchers with a track-record of significant research achievements in the last 10 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets well-established, leading researchers: emphasis on recent (last 10 years) significant achievements. Selection hinges on past high-level accomplishments and the proposed frontier research.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Proof of Concept eligibility & purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for researchers who have already received an ERC grant for their frontier research project and now want to explore the commercial or societal potential of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only open to prior ERC grantees; focused on activities translating or valorising ERC-funded research (commercial/societal potential). Check call documents for allowable activities and timing relative to the original ERC grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: ERC Synergy Grants eligibility & team composition
rubrics_metrics.description: These grants are for two to maximum four researchers working together and bringing different skills and resources to tackle ambitious research problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a small team (2–4 PIs) with complementary skills/resources aimed at high-risk, high-gain ambitious problems. Team composition, synergy between members, and the joint ambition of the project are key selection considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult national contact points for applicant support
rubrics_metrics.description: National contact points: There is one based in every EU and Associated Country, as well as in some countries outside Europe. They are designated to help applicants out in their own countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First-line resource for prospective applicants seeking country-specific guidance on ERC applications. Contact them early for procedural, eligibility and practical advice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the Work Programme and Information for Applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents and publications: If you are considering applying, you'll have several key documents to refer to, like the Work Programme and the Information for Applicants. These highlight the specifics of the calls every year...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These official documents contain call-specific rules, eligibility details, evaluation procedures, and submission requirements — they are authoritative and must be followed when preparing an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Have a question about your ERC application? Chances are you’re not alone. Throughout the years, we have collected some of the most frequently asked questions to guide you through the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FAQ to resolve common doubts about eligibility, application components, submission procedures and evaluation. Useful before contacting support to save time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for non-EU researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: For non EU-researchers: If you are a researcher from outside the EU and you wish to apply check out some of the things you should consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-EU applicants should review the specific practical and eligibility considerations mentioned by ERC (e.g., participation, host institution rules, mobility); consult national contact points and official guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from ERC explanatory videos and common-mistake guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC Classes: This series of 5 explanatory videos will give you concrete information about the ERC application process, including frequently made mistakes, tips and rumours. Step-by-step: For a short introduction to ERC grants, watch our step-by-step video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch ERC-produced videos to understand process steps, common pitfalls, and practical tips when preparing an application. These resources highlight recurring mistakes and reviewer expectations.
